section.title: Diabetic Kidney Disease - Pathogenesis and Staging

sections.section: Diabetic kidney disease (diabetic nephropathy) is a major microvascular complication occurring in approximately 30% to 40% of patients with long-standing diabetes. Hyperglycemia induces advanced glycation end-products, glomerular hyperfiltration, renal mesangial expansion, and progressive glomerulosclerosis. Early disease is typically asymptomatic and characterized by persistent microalbuminuria (urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio [UACR] between 30 and 300 mg/g). Advanced stages progress to macroalbuminuria (UACR > 300 mg/g) and a relentless decline in estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2), culminating in end-stage renal disease (ESRD).

section.title: Diabetic Kidney Disease - Screening and Renoprotective Therapy

sections.section: Annual screening for all diabetic patients consists of spot urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) alongside serum creatinine and eGFR calculation. First-line renoprotective pharmacological therapy includes Angiotensin Converting Enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or Angiotensin Receptor Blockers (ARBs), particularly in hypertensive individuals with albuminuria. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors significantly decelerate CKD progression and decrease cardiovascular morbidity in diabetic patients with eGFR down to 20 mL/min/1.73 m2. Non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (such as Finerenone) offer added renal protection.
